pr_title: RFC: API Change: PWM: add support for inverted PWM signals
pr_body:
Add support for requesting an inverted PWM pulse (active-low) when setting up the period and pulse width of a PWM pin. This is useful when driving external, active-low circuitry with a PWM signal.

You can do a "poor man" inverted PWM pulse just by "inverting" the pulse width, but without proper API support for inverted PWM signals it is not possible to do edge-aligned PWM with either a mix of active-low/active-high or any number of active-low PWM signals (which is often needed for motor control).

This PR updates all in-tree PWM controller drivers to match the new API signature. The NXP Kinetis FlexTimer (FTM) PWM controller driver has furthermore been updated to support PWM flags set through the device tree (as an example implementation).

The following in-tree samples have been updated to support PWM flags:
- samples/basic/blink_led
- samples/basic/fade_led
- samples/basic/rgb_led

Also, the PWM shell commands has been updated to allow specifying PWM flags. All other in-tree PWM consumers are updated to pass a flags value of 0.

The goal is to enable specification of PWM signal polarity through the device tree for supporting PWM controllers (e.g. using `pwms = <&pwm0 1 PWM_POLARITY_INVERTED>;` for PWM controller 0 channel/pin 1). Please see the included changes for the FTM PWM driver for examples.

Closes #21384
pr_comments:
The following PWM drivers can easily be updated to support this new API:
- `pwm_nrfx.c` (already supports inverted PWM signals through custom DTS properties)
- `pwm_mcux_ftm.c` (implemented as part of this PR as an example of the new API)

I expect other PWM peripherals already support setting PWM signal polarity. If a given PWM peripheral does not have hardware support for inverted signals, it may be possible to handle it within the driver itself.

As per API meeting, there are no major concerns with the change but the PWM API is currently marked as stable, which would force us to deprecate the current functions. This needs discussion at the TSC level to decide whether moving an API from stable to unstable is warranted (coupled with other examples in the tree).

Input to the next API meeting: According to our [API Lifecycle documentation](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/development_process/api_lifecycle.html#stable), non-backwards compatible changes to a stable API (The PWM API is currently marked as stable) can be done but must be mentioned in the release notes. The documentation also says that "Backwards-compatibility [for a stable API] will be maintained if reasonable".

issue_context.title: RFC: API Change: PWM: add support for inverted PWM signals
issue_context.body:
## Introduction

The Zephyr PWM API currently lacks a way of  requesting an inverted PWM pulse (active-low) when setting up the period and pulse width of a PWM pin. This is useful when driving external, active-low circuitry with a PWM signal.

### Problem description

The current Zephyr PWM API only allows for a "poor mans" inverted PWM pulse by "inverting" the pulse width, but without proper API support for inverted PWM signals it is not possible to do edge-aligned PWM with either a mix of active-low/active-high or any number of active-low PWM signals (which is often needed for motor control).

Some PWM signals will always need to be driven inverted ("active-low"), e.g. LEDs where the current is sourced from VCC and sinked into the SoC. Other PWM signals sometimes needs to be driven with normal polarity and at other times with inverted polarity (e.g. for motor control applications).

The above calls for both a way to specify PWM polarity for a given PWM client/consumer in the device tree (compile-time) and to be able to specify the polarity through the PWM API (run-time).

### Proposed change

Please see PR #20657 for the proposed changes.

## Detailed RFC

Please see PR #20657 for the details.

### Proposed change (Detailed)

Please see PR #20657 for the detailed proposed changes.

### Dependencies

Upon accepting this change, out-of-tree device trees needs to updated to specify PWM flags for any PWM clients/consumers referencing PWM controller drivers which now support flags.

Furthermore, all calls to the PWM API functions needs to changed to match the new function prototypes (e.g. by passing a 0 for the flags parameter).

Any out-of-tree PWM controller drivers will also need to be updated to match the new PWM API function prototypes.

### Concerns and Unresolved Questions

None so far.

## Alternatives

None to my knowledge.
comments:
thx for pushing it.
I was asking about the pwm polarity on slack.
My practical case is the pwm generation for an RGB LED. Because of resistors the board comes up after init with all 3 LEDs with maximum brightness. So I was looking for a solution and figured out that the sm32 port of the pwm driver(realized via TIM) does not support reversed polarity. My stm32f412 supports that and this stuff is somehow easy addable via LL/HAL.

review_comments: We generally want to be compatible with Linux DTS and Linux [pwm/pwm.h](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/blob/master/include/dt-bindings/pwm/pwm.h) doesn't define `PWM_POLARITY_NORMAL`. There is only `PWM_POLARITY_INVERTED`. Flags with value 0 tend to cause problems when used in the driver code. On the other hand GPIO bindings, which are somehow similar, do specify a flag to indicate normal polarity.

In case of GPIO API to specify which flags are supported we mention the name of the section, as defined by the doxygen entry. In this case that would be 'PWM polarity flags'. In the future we could add a link behind the text.
